learn: Music is organised sound. Sound is made by vibrations travelling through the air.
Pitch is how high or low a sound is. Faster vibrations make higher pitches.
Musicians name pitches with letters: A, B, C, D, E, F, G.
lessons.try: Stretch a rubber band and pluck it tight and loose to hear pitch change.

learn: Rhythm is the pattern of long and short sounds. The beat is the steady pulse.
Tempo is the speed of the beat: largo is slow, allegro is fast.
Dynamics are how loud or soft: piano (soft), forte (loud).
check: The steady pulse in music is the...
lessons.try: Clap a rhythm at three different tempos.

learn: Timbre is the special tone colour of a sound: a flute sounds different from a trumpet on the same note.
Texture describes how many layers of sound there are: thin or thick.
Harmony is two or more pitches sounding together.
lessons.try: Listen to a song and name the layers you hear.

learn: A whole note lasts four beats, a half note two, a quarter note one and an eighth note half a beat.
Two eighth notes equal one quarter note.
Rests are silences with matching values.
lessons.try: Clap a rhythm of quarter, half and eighth notes.

learn: A time signature shows how many beats are in each measure.
In 4/4, there are four quarter-note beats per measure. In 3/4, three beats: waltz time.
Bar lines divide music into measures.
lessons.try: Conduct a pattern in 3/4 and 4/4.

learn: A dot adds half the note's value: a dotted half note lasts three beats.
Syncopation places accents on weak beats or between beats.
Syncopation is common in jazz, ragtime and pop.
lessons.try: Listen to Scott Joplin's "The Entertainer" (1902) and clap the syncopation.

learn: Music is written on a staff of five lines and four spaces.
The treble clef is for higher notes; the bass clef is for lower notes.
Notes higher on the staff are higher in pitch.
check: The treble clef is for ___ notes.
Notes higher on the staff sound...
lessons.try: Draw a treble and bass clef.

learn: Treble clef lines from bottom to top: E, G, B, D, F ("Every Good Boy Does Fine").
Spaces spell F, A, C, E ("FACE").
Middle C sits on a short ledger line below the staff.
check: The bottom line of the treble clef is...
lessons.try: Name the notes in a short melody.

learn: Bass clef lines: G, B, D, F, A ("Good Boys Do Fine Always").
Bass clef spaces: A, C, E, G ("All Cows Eat Grass").
Pianists read both clefs at once on a grand staff.
check: The bottom line of the bass clef is...
lessons.try: Write your initials in bass-clef notes if possible.

learn: A scale is a series of notes going up or down in order.
The major scale follows the pattern whole, whole, half, whole, whole, whole, half.
C major uses only the white keys on a piano: C D E F G A B C.
check: A scale is a series of notes...
The major scale pattern ends with a...
lessons.try: Play or sing a C major scale.

learn: Minor scales often sound sad, dark or mysterious.
The natural minor scale lowers the 3rd, 6th and 7th notes of the major.
A minor uses only the white keys from A to A.
lessons.try: Compare a major and minor version of the same melody.

learn: A melody is a sequence of pitches that makes a musical idea.
Melodies move by step (next note) or by leap (skipping notes).
A phrase is a musical sentence, often four or eight bars.
check: A melody that moves to the next note moves by...
lessons.try: Compose a four-bar melody that moves by step and leap.

learn: String instruments make sound with vibrating strings: violin, viola, cello, double bass, harp.
Woodwinds use air across an edge or through a reed: flute, clarinet, oboe, bassoon.
The bigger the instrument, usually the lower its pitch.
lessons.try: Listen to a piece and identify string and woodwind sounds.

learn: Brass players buzz their lips into a mouthpiece: trumpet, French horn, trombone, tuba.
Percussion is struck, shaken or scraped: timpani, snare drum, xylophone, cymbals.
Some percussion plays pitches (xylophone); some doesn't (snare drum).
check: The lowest brass instrument is the...
lessons.try: Make a homemade percussion instrument.

learn: An orchestra has four sections: strings, woodwinds, brass and percussion.
The conductor leads with a baton, setting tempo and dynamics.
Sergei Prokofiev's "Peter and the Wolf" (1936) introduces instruments as characters.
check: The leader of an orchestra is the...
The largest section is usually the...
lessons.try: Listen to a performance and match instruments to characters.

learn: Form is the structure of a piece of music.
Binary form has two sections: AB.
Ternary form returns to the first section: ABA.
lessons.try: Listen to a piece and label its sections.

learn: Rondo form returns to A between contrasting sections: ABACA.
Theme and variations states a melody and then changes it in different ways.
Mozart wrote variations on "Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star".
lessons.try: Make three variations of a simple tune by changing rhythm, tempo or dynamics.

learn: Popular songs often use verse-chorus form.
Verses tell the story with changing words; the chorus repeats.
A bridge adds contrast before the final chorus.
check: The repeated part of a song is the...
lessons.try: Map the form of a favourite song.

learn: Dynamics range from pp (pianissimo, very soft) to ff (fortissimo, very loud).
mp is medium soft; mf is medium loud.
Dynamics bring feeling to music.
lessons.try: Sing a song with four different dynamic levels.

learn: Crescendo means gradually louder; decrescendo (or diminuendo) means gradually softer.
They are shown with a hairpin symbol opening or closing.
Maurice Ravel's "Boléro" (1928) is one long crescendo.
lessons.try: Listen to part of "Boléro" and describe the change.

learn: Staccato notes are short and detached; legato notes are smooth and connected.
Accents are notes played with extra emphasis.
Ritardando slows down; accelerando speeds up.
lessons.try: Play a melody staccato, then legato.

learn: Many West African traditions use drums like the djembe and call-and-response singing.
Polyrhythms layer different rhythms at the same time.
Caribbean steelpan music began in Trinidad and Tobago.
lessons.try: Perform a call-and-response song as a class.

learn: Indian classical music uses ragas (melody patterns) and talas (rhythm cycles); the sitar and tabla are common.
Japanese music includes the koto (a long zither) and taiko drums.
Indonesian gamelan uses bronze gongs and metallophones.
lessons.try: Listen to a gamelan piece and describe its sound.

learn: Mariachi music from Mexico uses violins, trumpets and guitars.
Celtic music from Ireland and Scotland uses fiddles, pipes and the bodhrán drum.
Brazilian samba features lively drums for Carnival.
lessons.try: Compare two world music styles in a short chart.

learn: Spirituals were religious songs created by enslaved African Americans, often with hidden meanings.
The blues grew in the American South around 1900, with a 12-bar form and "blue notes".
Ragtime used syncopated piano rhythms.
check: The blues often uses a ___-bar form.
lessons.try: Sing a spiritual such as "Swing Low, Sweet Chariot".

learn: Jazz grew in New Orleans in the early 1900s, mixing blues, ragtime and brass bands.
Improvisation, making up music on the spot, is central to jazz.
Louis Armstrong was a famous trumpet player and singer.
check: Making up music on the spot is...
lessons.try: Improvise a short rhythm on a desk or drum.

learn: Folk songs are passed down by people, often telling stories of daily life.
Country music grew from Appalachian folk and uses fiddles and guitars.
Rock and roll in the 1950s mixed blues, country and gospel.
check: Rock and roll began in the...
lessons.try: Make a timeline of American music styles.

learn: Composers start with an idea: a rhythm, a melody or a feeling.
Use repetition and contrast to build a piece.
Write it down using notation or record it.
check: A composition can start with a...
lessons.try: Compose an eight-bar piece using the keyboard in the music room.

learn: Practise a little every day rather than a lot once a week.
Practise slowly at first, then speed up.
Break hard parts into small sections.
lessons.try: Make a practice plan for one week.

learn: Performers prepare, warm up and focus on communicating the music.
Stage fright is normal; deep breaths help.
Good audiences listen quietly and applaud at the end of a piece.
lessons.try: Perform a short piece for family or classmates.
